description: The provided chart is a radial or donut-style diagram illustrating the relative emphasis or scoring of various capabilities in the context of language models following entangled, multi-turn instructions — as referenced in the paper “Can Language Models Follow Multiple Turns of Entangled Instructions.” The chart is divided into ten outer segments, each labeled with a specific capability and an associated numerical value, suggesting a scoring or weighting system. These outer segments are grouped into four larger inner segments, each representing a higher-level functional category: “Contradiction Resolution” (reddish-brown, encompassing Prioritization and Personalization), “Context Tracking” (dark blue, covering Triggering and Recursive Reasoning), “Context Retrieving” (dark green, including Dynamic Environment, Memorization, and Dynamic Instruction), and an unlabeled green segment (Multitasking and Privacy Protection). The values assigned to each outer segment are: Prioritization (100), Personalization (100), Privacy Protection (111), Multitasking (160), Dynamic Instruction (100), Memorization (100), Dynamic Environment (100), Recursive Reasoning (110), Triggering (100). The largest value, 160, is assigned to Multitasking, indicating it is the most heavily weighted capability in this framework. The chart uses distinct colors for each segment and includes clear labels with connecting lines for readability, but does not display percentages or a legend — the values appear to be absolute scores rather than proportions of a whole. The visual structure implies a hierarchical organization of cognitive or functional capacities required for complex instruction-following in language models.
